articles.title: Bucs Name UDFA as QB2 amid Baker Mayfield's Contract Negotiations, New NFL Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have reportedly settled on their backup quarterback.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have reportedly settled on their backup quarterback.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday that Jalon Daniels will back up Baker Mayfield—who has an uncertain long-term future with the team because of his own contract situation—to start the 2026 campaign.

Daniels joined the Buccaneers as an undrafted free agent with a signing bonus of $25,000, but Rapoport noted he "impressed throughout camp" and "earned" the role.

Tampa Bay signed Jake Browning this offseason after he started 10 games for the Cincinnati Bengals the past three seasons when Joe Burrow was injured. Browning was presumably going to be Mayfield's backup just like he was for Burrow in Cincinnati but was unable to beat out Daniels for the job.

However, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Browning was released Sunday with Daniels as the backup moving forward.

While Daniels dealt with injuries early in his collegiate career with Kansas even amid a breakout 2022 campaign, he appeared in 12 games in each of the last two seasons for the Jayhawks.

He posted 14 touchdown passes to 12 interceptions in 2024 but showed significant improvement in 2025 while completing 62.1 percent of his passes for 2,531 yards, 22 touchdowns and seven interceptions to go with 404 yards and four scores on the ground.

Daniels earned praise for his leadership and work ethic at Kansas and wasted little time proving himself at the NFL level with Tampa Bay by earning the backup role despite joining the team as an undrafted free agent.

The signal-caller saw time in each of the NFC South team's three preseason games and performed as follows:

It wasn't just the passing, as he also ran for a touchdown during the win over the Jets.

As for Mayfield, the 2026 campaign is the final one on his contract. He said he plans on focusing on football during the season after he and the Buccaneers were unable to come to terms on a long-term deal, but there remains plenty of uncertainty.

But there is no longer uncertainty over who is going to be his backup when Tampa Bay opens the season against the Bengals on Sept. 13 at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Colts WR Keenan Allen arrested for DWI in Indianapolis: What happened to the 34-year-old veteran receiver?
articles.summary: NFL News: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen was arrested early Sunday morning in Indianapolis after police accused him of driving while intoxicated..
articles.body: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen was arrested early Sunday morning in Indianapolis after police accused him of driving while intoxicated. The arrest came just hours after the veteran receiver played in the Colts’ preseason finale against the Detroit Lions on Saturday. According to jail records, the 34-year-old was booked on two preliminary misdemeanor charges: OWI while endangering another person and DWI with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 or higher. Allen was taken into custody shortly after 1 a.m. ET. The charges are allegations, and Allen has not been convicted of either offense.What happened in Keenan Allen’s Indianapolis DWI arrest?The incident happened in downtown Indianapolis early Sunday morning. A representative for the Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department told TMZ that officers were conducting a traffic investigation in the 100 block of S. Meridian Street when Allen was taken into custody shortly after 1 a.m.Jail records list two misdemeanor allegations against the Colts wide receiver. One is for OWI while endangering another person, while the other involves driving with a blood alcohol concentration of 0.08 or higher.The available reports do not provide all the details about what happened before Allen was arrested. At this point, the allegations remain unresolved, and more information could come out as the legal process continues.The Colts have acknowledged the incident. According to ESPN, the team said it was “aware of the incident involving Keenan Allen last night” and was working to gather more information. The organization did not provide further comment.For now, the arrest itself does not mean Allen has been found guilty of any offense. The charges are allegations, and any further developments will depend on the legal process and information provided by authorities.Why is Keenan Allen’s arrest significant for the Indianapolis Colts?The arrest comes less than two weeks after Allen joined the Colts. Indianapolis signed the veteran wide receiver as a free agent on Aug. 19, bringing in a six-time Pro Bowler with 1,055 career receptions, 12,051 receiving yards and 70 touchdowns, according to the team.Allen also played for the Colts in their preseason finale against the Detroit Lions on Saturday, just hours before his arrest. He caught one pass for 24 yards in the game as Indianapolis wrapped up its preseason preparations.The 2026 season is Allen’s 14th in the NFL. He spent the first 11 seasons of his career with the Los Angeles Chargers after being selected by the team in the third round of the 2013 NFL Draft. He became one of the Chargers’ most reliable receivers and earned six Pro Bowl selections during his time with the team.Allen joined the Chicago Bears in 2024 before returning to the Chargers for the 2025 season. In his most recent season with Los Angeles, he recorded 81 catches for 777 yards and four touchdowns.Indianapolis then signed him this month, adding a veteran presence to its receiving group ahead of the 2026 regular season.The timing of the arrest makes the situation important for the Colts, who had only recently added Allen to their roster. For now, the team has said it is gathering more information about the incident. Any decision about Allen’s status with Indianapolis could depend on what emerges from the legal process and any additional information released by authorities.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Dolphins Trade for Packers QB Kyle McCord to Backup Willis After Quinn Ewers Deal, Return Revealed
articles.summary: After trading backup quarterback Quinn Ewers to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Miami Dolphins have quickly found his replacement Kyle McCord.
articles.body:
After trading backup quarterback Quinn Ewers to the Jacksonville Jaguars, the Miami Dolphins have quickly found his replacement Kyle McCord.

The Dolphins sent the extra 2028 sixth-round draft pick that they received in the Ewers deal to the Green Bay Packers to acquire quarterback Kyle McCord, who will serve as the backup to starting signal-caller Malik Willis.

ESPN's Adam Schefter first reported the deal.

The acquisition of McCord continues the Green Bay-to-Miami pipeline, as Willis also played for the Packers before heading to South Beach. Former Packers defensive coordinator Jeff Hafley is entering his first year as Dolphins head coach after being hired by new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan, who previously worked in Green Bay's front office for over two decades.

A sixth-round pick in the 2025 NFL draft, McCord began his career with the Philadelphia Eagles before joining the Packers earlier this offseason. The 23-year-old has become a hot commodity in recent weeks thanks to his strong performance in the preseason. He played the entirety of Friday's preseason finale against the Arizona Cardinals, completing 22 of his 35 passes for 226 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions in a 42-38 victory.

Schefter added that despite McCord's impressive preseason, the Packers already have veteran signal-caller Tyrod Taylor in place as the backup to starting quarterback Jordan Love. Rather than holding on to McCord and continuing to develop him, Green Bay opted to flip him for a future draft pick.

The Dolphins are expected to go through a rebuild year in 2026, so there's a chance that McCord will get to see the field at some point this season as Miami tries to evaluate its best course for the future under Hafley.

articles.title: Bucs cut Jake Browning, elevating UDFA Jalon Daniels to QB2 behind Baker Mayfield
articles.summary: Daniels started 45 games in college for Kansas, but the rookie has no regular-season experience.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers appear prepared for an undrafted free agent to back up quarterback Baker Mayfield.

The Bucs have released backup Jake Browning, who was signed early in free agency this offseason to be Mayfield's backup. That means undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels, who has impressed all summer, is currently the QB2 behind Mayfield.

The 6-foot, 208-pound Daniels, who played six years at Kansas, went 27-of-44 passing for 239 yards and a TD, and rushed 14 times for 37 yards and one more score in three preseason games this summer. He was especially sharp in the first two exhibitions, helping spark second-half comebacks against the New York Jets and Kansas City Chiefs.

The dual-threat Daniels might have initially been viewed as a longer-term project, coming off a college career where his accuracy and consistency drew concern from scouts. But he started impressing the Bucs' coaches as early as OTAs and minicamps, earning praise for his off-schedule playmaking and quick recognition skills, which earned him QB2 reps in camp.

Even with a shakier effort in the third preseason game, losing a fumble and completing 8 of 15 passes for 57 yards, the Bucs have been impressed with the rookie.

The Bucs still could look to add a veteran quarterback, with several expected to be released on cutdown day . But for now, Daniels is the next man up. Tampa Bay opens the season at the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 1.

Daniels started 45 games in college for the Jayhawks, throwing for 9,282 yards, 67 TDs and 31 interceptions on 61.5% completions. He also ran for 1,445 yards and 23 touchdowns.

Browning, 30, spent the previous five seasons in Cincinnati as Joe Burrow's backup, starting 10 career games. The Bucs gave him $400,000 in guaranteed money at signing. If he clears waivers, he could return to the practice squad and be Tampa's third QB on gamedays.

In his three seasons in Tampa, Mayfield has never missed a game. He's currently in the final year of his contract and is at odds with the Bucs over a future extension, saying he has ended negotiations with the team until after the season.

articles.title: Kubiak Blames Raiders WR for Fernando Mendoza's INT, Watch Video of Viral Play vs. 49ers
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza was inconsistent during Thursday's preseason loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak didn't place the blame on the rookie quarterback for his interception.
articles.body:
Fernando Mendoza was inconsistent during Thursday's preseason loss to the San Francisco 49ers, but Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak didn't place the blame on the rookie quarterback for his interception.

"I thought that was an excellent throw," Kubiak said, per Ted Nguyen of The Athletic. "He ripped it, just like we asked him to, on time. Yeah, it was a little bit high. Jalen's gotta make a play."

While the pass deflected off Jalen Nailor's hands, it was also high and appeared overthrown. It eventually fell in the waiting hands of 49ers linebacker Tatum Bethune, who intercepted it.

Mendoza was 7-of-14 for 57 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception to cap off a preseason that had its ups and downs.

He impressed against the Arizona Cardinals while going 10-of-16 for 97 yards, one touchdown and zero interceptions but struggled against the Houston Texans at 8-of-15 for 86 yards, zero touchdowns and one interception. The interception against the Texans was returned for a touchdown by Wade Woodaz.

Expectations are high for Mendoza as the No. 1 overall pick of the 2026 NFL draft who is coming off a Heisman Trophy and national championship during his final collegiate season at Indiana.

However, he will reportedly have time to ease into the NFL before he is under the spotlight as the presumed franchise quarterback in Las Vegas. Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports reported the Raiders are expected to name Kirk Cousins the starter for their Week 1 game against the Miami Dolphins.

That will give Cousins some time to learn under the veteran signal-caller and ideally clean up some of the mistakes he made during the preseason.

Even if his head coach doesn't believe one of those mistakes was his fault.

articles.title: 49ers' George Kittle Responds to Injury Rumors with Funny, NSFW Brad Pitt Video
articles.summary: When you're an All-Pro tight end, sometimes social media can be amusing.
articles.body:
When you're an All-Pro tight end, sometimes social media can be amusing.

San Francisco 49ers star George Kittle took to social media Sunday and relayed a NSFW response to an injury update featuring Brad Pitt that he found quite funny:

The video was in response to a Sunday report from ESPN's Adam Schefter that revealed Kittle has not suffered any setbacks as he recovers from the torn Achilles he suffered last season and is expected to practice during the upcoming week.

Schefter noted the tight end "has a legitimate chance to play" in San Francisco's Sept. 10 season opener against the Los Angeles Rams.

It seemed like everything was on track for Kittle when the 49ers activated him from the active/physically unable to perform list last Sunday.

However, there was some concern he may have suffered a setback when head coach Kyle Shanahan made a vague reference during a press conference that the seven-time Pro Bowler had "taken a step back" without offering much clarity.

Schefter's latest report and Kittle's response seemed to clear that up, which is notable since it came after a previous report suggesting the Iowa product was ahead of schedule:

Kittle suffered the torn Achilles on Jan. 11 during his team's playoff win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Returning to the field in approximately eight months is quite an impressive turnaround, but the latest indications are he will do just that.

It is welcome news for the 49ers, who would be far more dangerous on offense with their star tight end on the field against their division rivals. And given how competitive the NFC West figures to be with the 49ers, Seattle Seahawks and Rams all fighting for playoff spots, that opener is all the more important given the opponent.

Kittle finished last season with 57 catches for 628 yards and seven touchdowns and isn't far removed from his dominant 2024 campaign when he tallied 78 catches for 1,106 yards and eight touchdowns.

It was his fourth season of his career with more than 1,000 receiving yards, and he will look to return to that form in 2026 as he bounces back from his setback.

articles.title: Dolphins acquire Kyle McCord from Packers after depleting QB depth on NFL roster cutdown day
articles.summary: Miami adds McCord to back up Malik Willis after trading away Quinn Ewers and releasing Cam Miller and Mark Gronowski.
articles.body:
The Miami Dolphins have acquired quarterback Kyle McCord from the Green Bay Packers for a 2028 sixth-round draft pick.

McCord will be the backup to starting QB Malik Willis after Miami depleted its depth at the position. Miami signed Willis in the offseason to a three-year, $67.5 million deal , making him its quarterback of the future.

Over the weekend, Miami parted ways with all three of Willis' backup options.

The Dolphins traded Quinn Ewers to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Saturday and followed that up by waiving both Cam Miller and Mark Gronowski on Sunday.

Those moves left Willis as the only quarterback on the roster. NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported that Miami was interested in bringing Gronowski back to the practice squad if he clears waivers, but that still doesn't answer the question of who will back up Willis.

McCord was a sixth-round pick by the Philadelphia Eagles in the 2025 NFL Draft. He spent his rookie season on the team's practice squad. The 23-year-old QB was released in the offseason and landed with the Packers during training camp and the preseason.

Now, McCord gets the chance to back up Willis and likely start the season on the 53-man roster in Miami.

articles.title: Colts Wide Receiver Keenan Allen Arrested on Drunken Driving Charges
articles.summary: INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen was arrested Sunday on drunken driving charges.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS (AP) — Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen was arrested Sunday on drunken driving charges.

Allen, 34, was being held at the Marion County Arrestee Processing Center. The misdemeanor charges listed on the jail records were operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated and operating a motor vehicle while intoxicated — endangering person.

The Colts announced on Aug. 19 that they had agreed to a one-year contract with Allen, a six-time Pro Bowl selection. He had one catch for 24 yards during Saturday night's 25-16 preseason loss to Detroit.

"We are aware of the incident involving Keenan Allen last night," the Colts said in a statement. "We are in the process of gathering more information and have no further comment at this time."

A message was left seeking comment from Allen's agent.

Allen had 81 receptions for 777 yards and four touchdowns in 17 games with the Los Angeles Chargers last season. He ranks 13th in NFL history in receptions (1,055), 33rd in yards (12,051) and 52nd in TD catches (70).

articles.title: Packers Trade for Steelers' Kaleb Johnson, RB Posts IG Photo amid New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are trading running back Kaleb Johnson to the Green Bay Packers, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are trading running back Kaleb Johnson to the Green Bay Packers, according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

The Steelers will receive a 2028 sixth-round draft pick, per Tom Silverstein of the Milwaukee Journal-Sentinel .

Johnson, a third-round pick in the 2025 NFL draft, ran for 69 yards in 10 games as a rookie. He suited up for all three of Pittsburgh's preseason contests, going for 53 yards on 17 carries.

The 23-year-old signaled his move to Green Bay on social media shortly before Fowler broke the news:

A coaching change can cut both ways. Players on the fringes had the opportunity to enter the offseason with a clean slate for coach Mike McCarthy. However, those who had impressed his predecessor, Mike Tomlin, didn't have that same equity with the new staff coming in.

Trading Johnson after just one year doesn't represent a great return on the Steelers' investment, but it didn't look like there was a path for him in Pittsburgh:

This is part of a larger theme, one that helps explain why the organization hit a wall toward the end of the Tomlin era.

Green Bay, meanwhile, is making room for the former Iowa standout by cutting Pierre Strong Jr., according to the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel 's Tom Silverstein .

Johnson was the No. 39 overall player and third-best running back in Bleacher Report's final 2025 big board . As a junior, he led the Big Ten in rushing yards (1,537) and touchdown runs (21). He also averaged 5.5 yards per carry over three years with the Hawkeyes.

Pittsburgh surely wasn't the only team that saw potential in Johnson when he was coming out of college. Landing in Green Bay could help to kick-start his pro career.

articles.title: Jets Trade for Raiders OL in New NFL Rumors, Add Starting Experience Ahead of Season
articles.summary: The New York Jets reportedly bolstered their offensive line depth ahead of Sunday's 6 p.m. ET roster cut deadline.
articles.body:
The New York Jets reportedly bolstered their offensive line depth ahead of Sunday's 6 p.m. ET roster cut deadline.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported the Jets acquired center Jordan Meredith from the Las Vegas Raiders via trade. Meredith started a combined 19 games for Las Vegas the past two seasons but was likely going to be in a backup role in 2026.

There were also draft picks involved in the move:

Las Vegas made center Tyler Linderbaum the highest-paid center in the league with a three-year, $81 million deal this offseason, so Meredith was relegated to a bench role on the depth chart.

The Raiders at least got something back in return for him by trading him ahead of the roster cut deadline, although there may not be a starting role waiting in New York either considering Josh Myers is the starting center.

Myers started all 17 games in New York last season after starting at least 16 games in each of the previous three years for the Green Bay Packers.

If nothing else, Meredith gives the Jets a backup with starting experience. He started 11 games for the Raiders in 2025, although he wasn't especially effective.

Pro Football Focus gave him an overall player grade of 57.7 last season, which was 32nd of 40 eligible centers. Perhaps a change of scenery can help him improve as he looks to provide quality depth in New York.

articles.title: Cowboys Waive Shiyazh Pete After Viral Video of Locker Room Speech During NFL Preseason
articles.summary: Offensive lineman Shiyazh Pete turned heads this preseason with a moving speech after the Dallas Cowboys' win over the Arizona Cardinals, but he reportedly did not do enough to make the NFC East team's roster.
articles.body:
Offensive lineman Shiyazh Pete turned heads this preseason with a moving speech after the Dallas Cowboys' win over the Arizona Cardinals, but he reportedly did not do enough to make the NFC East team's roster.

ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Sunday the Cowboys are waiving Pete ahead of the 6 p.m. ET roster cut deadline.

While he was an undrafted free agent, he made national headlines after that game against the Cardinals with his speech.

"Fate brought us here as strangers, but this game, this star, this team will make us brothers," he said.

Pete started his collegiate career at New Mexico State and played for Kentucky during the 2025 campaign. He appeared in 12 games for the Wildcats and joined the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent.

Perhaps he will now have the opportunity to join a different team after Dallas released him Sunday.

articles.title: QB Dillon Gabriel will reportedly make Browns' 53-man roster
articles.summary: The Browns appear to be taking three quarterbacks into the regular season on their 53-man roster.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns are reportedly going to take three quarterbacks into the regular season on the team's 53-man roster.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Sunday afternoon that second-year quarterback Dillon Gabriel was expected to make the 53-man roster.

Gabriel spent the preseason as the No. 3 QB behind Deshaun Watson and Shedeur Sanders, who were duking it out for the starting gig.

New head coach Todd Monken named Watson the starter , which made Sanders the presumptive backup. This raised questions about what would happen to Gabriel.

The second-year QB made six starts as a rookie last season as Cleveland looked to see what it had in the 25-year-old. He, like the Browns overall, struggled, and while he was the starter, the team went 1-5.

Gabriel finished the season with 937 yards, 7 touchdowns and 2 interceptions. By comparison, Sanders started seven games in 2025 and led the team to a 3-4 record in that span. He had 1,400 yards, 7 touchdowns and 10 interceptions.

This will be the second straight year Cleveland has carried three quarterbacks on its 53-man roster into the regular season.

Last year, it was rookies Sanders and Gabriel, along with veteran QB Joe Flacco. After the Browns started 1-3, Cleveland turned to Gabriel in Week 5 before going with Sanders in Week 12.

Monken and the Browns hope that Watson rebounds this season, beginning with his Week 1 start at the Jacksonville Jaguars. If not, it could be another season where Cleveland is glad to have young depth to turn to on the roster.

articles.title: Steelers reportedly trading second-year RB Kaleb Johnson to Packers
articles.summary: Johnson, 23, was a third-round pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are trading running back Kaleb Johnson to the Green Bay Packers, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Johnson was selected by Pittsburgh in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft. As a rookie, he played in 10 games. In a crowded backfield consisting of Jaylen Warren and Kenny Gainwell, Johnson tallied only 28 carries for 69 yards.

While Gainwell left for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in free agency, Pittsburgh replaced him with Rico Dowdle. That reunited Dowdle with head coach Mike McCarthy, with whom he spent five years with the Dallas Cowboys from 2020 through 2024.

Johnson felt like the odd man out, and Green Bay took the chance to add to its running back room.

Packers starting running back Josh Jacobs was added to the commissioner's exempt list on Sunday afternoon. He will not be allowed to practice or play in games while on the list, and the league can still issue a suspension.

The Packers can develop Johnson and he could be someone the team turns to if Jacobs is handed a lengthy suspension at the start of the season.

With every team done with preseason games, the focus is on trimming 90-player preseason rosters down to a 53-man roster by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday.

Rather than cutting Johnson, Pittsburgh traded him to Green Bay, likely for some draft capital, though the return has not yet been reported.

In a corresponding move, the Packers waived RB Pierre Strong Jr., per NFL insider Jordan Schultz .

Along with Jacobs, Green Bay's running back room will consist of some combination of Johnson, MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks, Damien Martinez and Jaden Nixon, depending on what other roster cuts the team makes Sunday.

For Pittsburgh, it appears that Warren and Dowdle will lead the backfield. After them, the Steelers will have Travis Horner, Lew Nichols, and Eli Heidenreich.

articles.title: NFL places Packers RB Josh Jacobs on commissioner exempt list after offseason domestic abuse arrest
articles.summary: Josh Jacobs was arrested in May after an incident in Wisconsin.
articles.body:
Running back Josh Jacobs will miss the start of the 2026 NFL season this fall.

The NFL placed the Green Bay Packer on the commissioner exempt list on Sunday after his arrest earlier this year, the league announced.

Jacobs will not be allowed to practice or play for the Packers while he is on the list, though he will continue to be paid. It is unclear how long he will be on the exempt list. The league can still issue a suspension.

The Packers open the season against the Minnesota Vikings on Sept. 13.

"Josh Jacobs has been placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List, which is an administrative procedure used by the NFL while a matter is being reviewed. It is not a final determination," Jacobs' representation said in a statement, via the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport . "Josh respects the NFL process, the Packers, and his coaches and teammates. He looks forward to his return to the team and the NFL."

Jacobs was arrested in Wisconsin in May and was levied five different charges related to domestic abuse. He was formally charged with battery and criminal damage to property last week, both of which are misdemeanors in Wisconsin.

Specifics of the incident aren't publicly unknown, and Jacobs denied the allegations made against him. Jacobs was in police custody for about a day before he was released.

Jacobs then returned to the team and started preparing for the new season as normal. The league launched an investigation into the matter.

While things were pending for several months, the Packers knew that a suspension or a spot on the exempt list was a possibility.

"We've obviously been preparing for that in case that happens," general manager Brian Gutekunst said on Wednesday . "But at the same time, I feel really good about the guys we have in that room."

Jacobs had 929 rushing yards and 14 total touchdowns last season, his second with the Packers after starting his career with the Las Vegas Raiders. He signed a four-year, $48 million deal with the Packers in free agency ahead of the 2024 campaign.

Jacobs and the Packers went 9-7-1 last season and made the postseason for a third straight campaign, though they were knocked out in the wild-card round of the playoffs against the rival Chicago Bears.

With Jacobs now sidelined, his workload is likely going to fall to Chris Brooks and MarShawn Lloyd. Brooks has spent the last two seasons with the Packers, and he had 106 rushing yards on 27 attempts last fall. Lloyd, who was selected in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft, has appeared in only one game due to various injuries.

The Packers also reportedly made a move Sunday to trade for running back Kaleb Johnson in a deal with the Pittsburgh Steelers. Johnson, who was selected in the third round of the 2025 NFL Draft, had 69 rushing yards on 28 carries with the Steelers.

While the Packers are undoubtedly in a much better spot when Jacobs is around, it may be a while before he's able to take the field for them again this season.

articles.title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs Placed on Commissioner's Exempt List by NFL
articles.summary: The NFL placed Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list, according to Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network.
articles.body:
The NFL placed Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list, according to Ian Rapoport of ESPN and NFL Network.

Jacobs is unable to practice or attend games while on the list.

The Ringer's Tom Pelissero shared a statement from Jacobs' attorneys: "Josh Jacobs has been placed on the Commissioner's Exempt List, which is an administrative procedure used by the NFL while a matter is being reviewed. It is not a final determination. Josh respects the NFL process, the Packers, and his Coaches and Teammates. He looks forward to his return to the team and the NFL."

Players on the exempt list continue to receive their salary but are ineligible from playing or practicing with their team. In the case of Jacobs, that represents a significant blow to Green Bay's offense.

The three-time Pro Bowler's performance dipped a bit in 2025. He failed to crack 1,000 rushing yards (929) and saw his yards per carry fall from 4.4 to 4.0.

There isn't a clear replacement for Jacobs in the backfield, though.

MarShawn Lloyd, a third-round pick in the 2024 draft, has logged just six total carries in the regular season, and he didn't see the field at all in 2025. Chris Brooks' NFL resume isn't much better. Across three seasons, he has 395 yards and one touchdown on the ground.

The Packers are also adding Kaleb Johnson in a trade from the Pittsburgh Steelers, per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler . Johnson, a third-rounder in 2025, led the Big Ten in rushing yards (1,537) and touchdown runs (21) as a junior. He'll now be firmly in the mix to earn carries in Green Bay.

articles.title: Broncos LB Jonathon Cooper Placed on Commissioner's Exempt List by NFL
articles.summary: The NFL placed Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper on the Commissioner's Exempt list on Sunday, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
The NFL placed Denver Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper on the Commissioner's Exempt list on Sunday, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport .

Cooper will be barred from practicing or attending games while he's on the list.

The Associated Press reported that Cooper was arrested in June on domestic violence charges.

articles.title: 2026 Fantasy Football Mock Draft, Overall Draft Strategy and Printable Cheat Sheet
articles.summary: We're now just over a week away from the start of the 2025 NFL regular season. The Seattle Seahawks will begin their title defense on Wednesday, September 9, and from there, the season will be off and running.
articles.body:
We're now just over a week away from the start of the 2025 NFL regular season. The Seattle Seahawks will begin their title defense on Wednesday, September 9, and from there, the season will be off and running.

In the coming days, many fantasy managers in season-long redraft leagues will be looking to cram. We're here to help with that process by diving into a three-round point-per-reception (PPR) mock draft conducted with FantasyPros' Mock Draft Simulator . We'll highlight any intriguing trends and examine relevant 2026 draft strategies along the way before providing a top-30 cheat sheet for early draft selections.

Ideally, our analysis will help you know what to expect when it's time for your live draft, though we'd recommend conducting a few practice drafts of your own.

Those looking for a cheat sheet for additional draft-day help should check out the printable and fully customizable sheet from The Athletic's Jake Ciely .

Jaxon Smith-Njigba, WR, Seattle Seahawks

Christian McCaffrey, RB, San Francisco 49ers

There weren't too many surprises in the first round of this mock. Ja'Marr Chase continues to trend ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba as WR 1 in most leagues, and both Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson are regularly top-four selections.

Strategically, focusing on a high-volume running back like Gibbs, Robinson, or Jonathan Taylor in the first round makes a ton of sense in 2026. The first and second RB tiers are great, but there's a massive drop-off at the position after that.

A No. 1 receiver like Smith-Njigba, Puka Nacua, or Justin Jefferson is certainly worth a pick in the first round. However, managers are more likely to find acceptable Rounds 3-6 at WR than at RB. Don't be afraid to give running backs a bit of a bump in your pre-draft rankings.

The one curious thing about this mock first round was the fact that Christian McCaffrey went ahead of Taylor and in the top half of the round. Based on his 2025 production, McCaffrey is worth that, but he's still a 30-year-old back coming off a 413-touch season, which makes him a legitimate injury risk.

Omarion Hampton, RB, Los Angeles Chargers

Kenneth Walker III, RB, Kansas City Chiefs

Over half of the Round 2 selections in this mock were used on running backs, and that falls in line with early 2026 strategies. As previously mentioned, top running backs are at a premium this year, while there is a wide second tier of wide receivers.

A couple of picks in this round of the mock are questionable, however.

Kenneth Walker III probably belongs in the next tier of RBs, along with backs like Javonte Williams and Travis Etienne Jr. He is the reigning Super Bowl MVP, but he's also in a new offense with the Kansas City Chiefs and has a notable injury history.

Managers should also think twice about treating Drake London like a borderline first-round pick. He has the talent to be a top-10 WR, but the Atlanta Falcons have serious questions at quarterback. It's also worth noting that new head coach Kevin Stefanski runs an offense that rarely force-feeds the football to any one wide receiver.

Williams was the only RB to go in Round 3, and he sits at the top of the position's third tier. We also saw the first tight ends and quarterbacks come off the board in Round 3.

Brock Bowers and Trey McBride are proven players and elite fantasy options worth targeting in this range. Colston Loveland was promising as a rookie last season but is a bit more of a speculative pick in Round 3.

Of course, there's nothing wrong with taking a swing on a player with legitimate upside. In Loveland's case, the departure of receiver D.J. Moore could lead to an even more prominent role in the Chicago Bears' offense. When betting on upside, though, always remember that it doesn't come with a guarantee.

Loveland might match the production of Bowers and McBride, but his numbers could also fall in line with TEs drafted several rounds after him. The same probably isn't true for quarterbacks Josh Allen and Lamar Jackson, though the gap may not be sizeable enough to justify using a third-round pick on a QB.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba, RB, Seattle Seahawks

articles.title: Will Levis Waived by Titans in New NFL Rumors, Top Landing Spots for QB in Free Agency
articles.summary: Will Levis' time with the Tennessee Titans is reportedly over.
articles.body:
Will Levis' time with the Tennessee Titans is reportedly over.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Sunday the Titans waived the quarterback before the 6 p.m. ET roster cut deadline. He entered the league as a second-round pick in the 2023 NFL draft but never lived up to expectations.

Here are some potential landing spots now that Levis is heading to free agency:

It should be noted none of these landing spots are for a starting role.

Levis had his chance as a starter for the Titans and largely struggled with a 5-16 record across the 2023 and 2024 seasons. His QBR in his 12 games in 2024 of 25.2 was 36th in the league, per Pro Football Reference .

That means teams that either need backup depth or could give him an opportunity to work with an offensive-minded coach to revive his career figure to be his best landing spots.

The Washington Commanders stand out with Marcus Mariota dealing with a knee injury this preseason. Having enough playable backup depth is important in Washington after Jayden Daniels was limited to seven games last season, and Levis could at least provide an insurance policy.

Perhaps he could end up with the Green Bay Packers as well.

Green Bay traded away a depth piece in Kyle McCord and would give Levis an opportunity to work with head coach Matt LaFleur. LaFleur has an offensive background and is known for his ability to get the best out of his quarterbacks, so perhaps he could help Levis turn things around moving forward.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers could also use more depth after they released veteran Jake Browning, per ESPN's Adam Schefter .

Undrafted free agent Jalon Daniels becoming the backup behind Baker Mayfield is an impressive story, but Levis would at least give the Buccaneers someone who has game experience behind their starter.

articles.title: Broncos' Jonathon Cooper to be placed on NFL commissioner's exempt list: Reports
articles.summary: Broncos star Jonathon Cooper is being placed on the NFL commissioner's exempt list after a pair of offseason arrests relating to domestic violence.
articles.body:
The NFL is placing Jonathon Cooper on the commissioner's exempt list, according to multiple reports .

It comes after an offseason of issues for the Denver Broncos star. Cooper was was arrested twice in just one week for charges of domestic violence.

Cooper was originally arrested on June 4 on suspicion of domestic violence and one count of criminal mischief, jail records show. He was arrested for a second time on June 11 , which brought four new charges: two for domestic violence, one for harassment (repeated telephone calls) and one for violation of a protection order from his initial arrest on Thursday, June 4.

He was later excused from Denver's mandatory minicamp, which head coach Sean Payton announced on June 16.

"We've excused him from this minicamp," Payton told reporters . "He's taking this time, obviously, he's got to work on himself. The club is very much in tune to the league office, local authorities here, and we've had several meetings.

"Clearly, from an ownership standpoint, head coach, organizationally, there's a bar we have and an expectation we have that's very high. We'll consider all that as we continue to gather information."

It's unclear how long Cooper will be on the exempt list.

He signed a four-year, $60 million contract extension with the Broncos in Nov. 2024.

NFL players on the move during 2026 offseason

The commissioner's exempt list is a form of paid administrative leave the NFL designates for players in specific circumstances, according to the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy.

When a player is formally charged with a felony offense or a crime of violence;

When an investigation leads the Commissioner to believe a player may have violated the Personal Conduct Policy by committing any prohibited conduct;

In cases where a violation relating to a crime of violence is alleged but further investigation is required.

Players are still paid while on the commissioner's exempt list and can participate in certain team activities. However, they are unable to participate in practice or attend games, as the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy outlines.

"A player who is placed on the Commissioner Exempt List may not practice or attend games, but upon request and with the club's permission he may be present at the club's facility on a reasonable basis for meetings, individual workouts, therapy and rehabilitation, and other permitted non-football activities," the policy reads.

articles.title: Titans reportedly waive former second-round pick Will Levis
articles.summary: Levis was heading into the final year of his rookie deal and now gets a fresh start.
articles.body:
The Tennessee Titans are reportedly waiving quarterback Will Levis, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero .

Levis was drafted in the second round of the 2023 NFL Draft by Tennessee. He got the chance to start 21 games between the 2023 and 2024 seasons, but was replaced after the Titans selected Cam Ward with the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler added to Pelissero's report that the quarterback requested his release so that he could get a fresh start with a new team.

Since Levis was drafted in the second round, he did not have a fifth-year option available. As such, he was heading into the final year of his four-year contract with the Titans, but he will now be free to sign anywhere if he passes through waivers.

Levis made nine starts as a rookie in 2023. Tennessee had a 3-6 record in the games that he started, and he finished with 1,808 yards, 8 touchdowns, and 4 interceptions.

The Titans turned to their young quarterback again in 2024 for 12 games. Levis led them to a 2-10 record in that span and had 2,091 yards with 13 touchdowns and 12 interceptions.

He helped the franchise earn the No. 1 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft, but Tennessee opted to draft his replacement, Ward, who will start for the Titans again this season. Tennessee signed veteran Mitch Trubisky this offseason, who will back up Ward.

Levis requesting his release would not be a surprise. He went viral this offseason for saying in an interview that he "100% believed" he could still be a starter in the league and "there are not 32 quarterbacks in this league better than me."

Looking around the league, there are not too many obvious landing spots for Levis. A team could certainly claim or sign him, but the lone quarterback battle that hasn't been decided yet is with the Atlanta Falcons, who are deciding between Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix Jr.

Anything can happen, though, and Levis now gets the chance to bet on himself and sign with a new franchise for a fresh start.

articles.title: ‘Sean Payton was right’: J.J. McCarthy’s Vikings future takes a stunning turn as QB reunion talk grows
articles.summary: J. J. McCarthy’s Minnesota Vikings future has taken another twist, with speculation growing that the former first-round pick could be traded or released befo...
articles.body:
J.J. McCarthy's Minnesota Vikings future has taken another twist, with speculation growing that the former first-round pick could be traded or released before the start of the 2026 season.

The quarterback has been under increasing pressure following a difficult spell in Minnesota, while the Vikings have already named Kyler Murray their QB1 for the upcoming campaign.

Now, the possibility of McCarthy leaving has opened the door to a potential reunion with former Vikings quarterback Nick Mullens, who was released by the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday.

J.J. McCarthy's Vikings future remains uncertain

McCarthy missed his entire rookie season after tearing the meniscus in his right knee during pre-season and undergoing surgery.

He returned in 2025 but struggled for consistency, completing 140 of 243 passes for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions. He also rushed for 181 yards and four touchdowns across 10 games as Minnesota went 6-4 in his starts.

The Vikings have since moved ahead with Murray, leaving McCarthy's role unclear as roster cuts approach.

NFL analyst Paul Charchian was particularly critical of the situation, arguing that Minnesota's decision to move on from Sam Darnold in 2025 to keep McCarthy was another mistake.

'Tomorrow likely ends JJ McCarthy's time in Minnesota. Worse than getting nothing from the 2023 1.10, the team doubled down on him when they chose to let Sam Darnold walk. A brutal series of decisions with franchise-changing ramifications,' Charchian wrote.

He then added a blunt assessment of the quarterback's situation: 'Worst part, Sean Payton was right.'

Payton had previously claimed he used smoke screens to encourage Minnesota to trade up for McCarthy at No. 10 in the 2024 NFL Draft, allowing Denver to select Bo Nix at No. 12.

Meanwhile, The Athletic's Alec Lewis believes McCarthy could have played his last regular-season snap for the Vikings.

Nick Mullens emerges as a possible Vikings reunion

McCarthy's uncertain future comes as Mullens suddenly becomes available.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported that Jacksonville released the veteran quarterback one day after trading for Quinn Ewers. ESPN's Kevin Seifert responded with an eyes emoji, although he stressed that he did not know anything about a possible Vikings reunion.

Mullens previously spent three seasons in Minnesota under Kevin O'Connell, appearing in 13 games and making three starts.

He completed 70.3 per cent of his passes for 1,568 yards, eight touchdowns and nine interceptions during that spell.

With quarterback spots still available around the league, Mullens could quickly find another home. For Minnesota, however, his sudden availability adds another option if the Vikings decide McCarthy's time with the franchise is over.
